input.command: ls -R | grep -v node_modules | head -50; cat -n src/api.ts
grep -rn "loadDashboard\|fetchCurrentUser\|fetchUserList\|unhandledrejection\|\.catch" src package.json; cat -n src/dashboard.ts | head -60

input.reason: The issue is real for the current-user fetch, but not for the user-list fetch. In src/api.ts, fetchCurrentUser (line 13) passes the response to json(), and json() throws `HTTP ${status}` for any non-2xx response (line 7). A network error from fetch also propagates. loadDashboard awaits fetchCurrentUser at line 27 with no try/catch. The only caller, mountDashboard in src/dashboard.ts:5, starts it with `void loadDashboard(...)` and attaches no .catch. So when /api/me fails, the promise rejection goes unhandled, render is never called, and the root element stays at "Loading..." forever. Nothing in the repo handles unhandledrejection. F02's claim about fetchUserList is wrong: lines 17-23 wrap the request in try/catch and return [] when !res.ok or on any exception, so it never throws. For the same reason, F03's "either one" is only half right. "Crash" overstates the effect: the page does not blow up, it just hangs on the loading text with no error shown.
input.failure_scenario: A user's session expires and GET /api/me returns 401. json() in src/api.ts:7 throws "HTTP 401", and the rejection passes through loadDashboard at line 27 to `void loadDashboard(...)` in src/dashboard.ts:5, where nothing catches it. The rejection goes unhandled, render never runs, and the dashboard stays at "Loading..." with no error message and no redirect to login.
input.severity_reason: This only happens when /api/me fails (expired session, server error or network failure), which is a failure path, not the normal flow. The result is a dashboard stuck on "Loading..." plus an unhandled rejection. No data is lost or corrupted and there is no security impact. The user-list half of the claim is false because fetchUserList already handles its errors.
